repair_verification.evidence: server/index.js coreV0ServiceForRequest constructs the PostgreSQL production adapter for the target route; A-02 and A-11 pass and the mock model is rejected in production.
server/memory-module-postgres.js upserts memory_commit_sequences before SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, so concurrent first writes serialize on a persisted row.
server/core-v0-postgres.js loadCoreRows reads subject, turns, bindings, commits and messages inside one REPEATABLE READ transaction.

server/core-v0-production.js prepares both owners: table plus required-column inspection for Core and Memory, DDL only under CORE_V0_AUTO_MIGRATE with an advisory migration lock, production never migrates, and a migration that cannot repair the structure still ends in a retryable CORE_V0_SCHEMA_NOT_READY with the absent tables and columns in error details.
The session message view reads core_v0_messages through a session-scoped bounded query and merges legacy rows for read parity; Core rows are never written back to JSON state (A-06).
server/memory-module-postgres.js contains no reference to Core state or Core tables; assistant receipt identity is owned by Core (A-07).
server/store.js exposes getApplicationPostgresPool and the adapter consumes it via getPool; no second pool is constructed on the target path (A-02).

advisories.statement: Schema readiness probes current_schema() only; tables hidden behind a multi-schema search_path report as missing.
advisories.recommendation: Fail-closed today. If a second schema is ever introduced, pin search_path in the pool configuration or resolve tables per schema.

advisories.statement: A successful readiness result is cached per pool for the process lifetime, so dropping tables underneath a running process is not observed until restart.
advisories.recommendation: Accepted trade-off: readiness must not probe on every request. Operational rollback deletes the process, not the schema.

advisories.statement: The bounded view truncates the merged legacy-plus-Core list to the newest limit entries, so a very large legacy backlog can push Core rows out of one page; channel counts stay correct because they aggregate in SQL.
advisories.recommendation: Legacy rows migrate per the R-003 plan; no action in this slice.

advisories.statement: Cross-turn messages committed within the same millisecond still order by application_message_id as a final tie-break; commit time is clamped strictly after turn admission, which covers the user/assistant pair of one turn.
advisories.recommendation: If cross-turn same-millisecond ordering ever matters, add a monotonic sequence column rather than extending time-based clamping.

advisories.statement: createCoreV0LocalAdapter does not run the tightened context requirement; it stays reachable only on the JSON development path, and production storage is enforced separately.
advisories.recommendation: Acceptable for the bounded local fallback; revisit if the local adapter is ever promoted.

steelman: The strongest case against closing is that readiness now inspects structure but still cannot prove constraint parity (uniqueness, foreign keys) inside each table. That risk is bounded because the same structural probe fails closed, write-time unique violations surface as explicit conflicts, and live locking behavior remains evidenced by R-003. The five acceptance-relevant behaviors - distinguishable schema policy, bounded session reads, request-scoped identity, unified error semantics, and the production mock prohibition - are each covered by executable checks.
overall: No blocking findings remain. All seven input findings are verified repaired, five advisories are recorded, and the executable gates are green: npm test (291 checks), npm run test:core-v0-production, npm run acceptance:core-v0-chat-turns (A-01..A-12), and the provenance checker. Production Auth/TLS and traffic promotion remain separate gates outside this package.
